tools.name: cli-conformance
tools.summary: Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.
tools.when:
Run this after adding a CLI, or when `npm run check:cli` fails. It answers two questions the
generated reference cannot: is anything claimed that does not exist, and is anything present
that was never declared.
tools.description:
npm run cli-conformance -- — Check that every operator CLI is registered and on the shared harness.

Run this after adding a CLI, or when `npm run check:cli` fails. It answers two questions the
generated reference cannot: is anything claimed that does not exist, and is anything present
that was never declared.

Reports MISSING (the manifest names a file that is gone), NOT_CONVERTED and
NO_ENTRYPOINT_GUARD (a tier A/B tool that is not on the harness) and UNTIERED (a CLI-shaped
file the manifest omits). The census currently walks scripts/ops only — see the 🛑 note in
lib/cli/census.ts before widening it.

Read-only. This command changes nothing.

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 130. For this command, 1 = at least one finding.

Examples:
  npm run check:cli
  npm run check:cli -- --tier a

format.description: Output format (default: json off a terminal)

tools.name: cli-reference
tools.summary: Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.
tools.when:
Run this after changing any tool's defineCommand() block — its summary, flags, examples or
subcommands. The generated files are committed, and `npm test` fails when they are stale, so
this is the fix for that failure. Never hand-edit the generated files.
tools.description:
npm run cli-reference -- — Regenerate the committed CLI documentation from the tools' own declarations.

Run this after changing any tool's defineCommand() block — its summary, flags, examples or
subcommands. The generated files are committed, and `npm test` fails when they are stale, so
this is the fix for that failure. Never hand-edit the generated files.

Writes <dir>/CLI_README.md (the full --help), docs/cli-reference.md (an index only) and
docs/cli-tools.json (the machine catalogue). Discovery is the registry in lib/cli/tiers.ts,
not a glob, and a file is statically checked for `export const cmd` / `defineCommand(` /
`import.meta.url` before it is imported — importing an unconverted tool would RUN it.

WRITES. Dry by default: without --apply nothing changes and the report says what would. Off a terminal --apply additionally requires --yes, or it refuses with exit 2.

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 130. For this command, 1 = generated files are stale (--check), or a listed tool could not be loaded.

Examples:
  npm run cli:reference
  npm run cli:reference -- --apply
  npm run cli:reference -- --check

check.description: Write nothing; exit 1 if any generated file is stale or a tool failed to load

format.description: Output format (default: json off a terminal)

apply.description: Actually write. Without it nothing changes and the report says what would.

yes.description: Confirm without prompting. Required alongside --apply when stdin is not a terminal.

tools.name: liveone__area__flows
tools.summary: The rolled-up source×load energy-flow matrix (the Sankey) for a period.
tools.when:
Use this to download WHERE an area's energy came from and went to over a period, with the
attributed cost/emissions/renewable legs — the multi-day rollup of the per-day Sankey.
tools.parentWhen:
Reach for this for the SEMANTIC layer: what an area is made of and what it measured. For the
physical/vendor layer use `device`; for what a dashboard shows use `dashboard`.
tools.description:
npm run liveone -- area flows — The rolled-up source×load energy-flow matrix (the Sankey) for a period.

Use this to download WHERE an area's energy came from and went to over a period, with the
attributed cost/emissions/renewable legs — the multi-day rollup of the per-day Sankey.

About `area` generally: Reach for this for the SEMANTIC layer: what an area is made of and what it measured. For the
physical/vendor layer use `device`; for what a dashboard shows use `dashboard`.

Reads the materialized per-day matrices (`flow_attr_1d` via /api/history) and folds them:
energy is a plain sum; each metric leg sums only the days where it is known, and carries a
known-kWh denominator so averages divide by known energy only. Windows are capped at 13
months (the 1d serving cap). The matrix is per-AREA — never sum a multi-device area with
its member devices.

Read-only. This command changes nothing.

Calls the deployed LiveOne API as the signed-in user. A missing, expired or revoked CLI token is exit 3.

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 130. For this command, 1 = no attributed flow for the window (the reason says why).

Examples:
  liveone area flows daylesford --last=90d
  liveone area flows daylesford --start=2026-01-01 --end=2026-06-30 --csv --out=flows.csv

area.description: An area: its ar_… id, integer handle, or display name

base-url.description: Target origin (default: your stored default, else https://www.liveone.energy) (origin)

per-day.description: Also carry the raw per-day matrices (CSV: one row per day×edge)

csv.description: Serialise as CSV, one row per source×load edge (to pipe raw CSV, add --format=human or --out)

out.description: Write the CSV/JSON to this file; stdout gets a summary (path)

format.description: Output format (default: json off a terminal)

tools.signature: liveone area flows <area> { --base-url?: string; --last?: string; --start?: string; --end?: string; --per-day?: boolean; --csv?: boolean; --out?: string }
